subject: LlamaWatch instrumentation & Redwood trace integration
messages:
From: Olivia Harper <olivia@llamawatch.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 6 Jan 2027 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Intro: LlamaWatch instrumentation - lightweight traces for LangChain/LlamaIndex

Hi Stephanie + Vanessa,

Hope you both had a great holiday. Quick intro — I run partnerships at LlamaWatch (we build low-overhead tracing and prompt observability for LangChain and LlamaIndex workloads). We’ve been accelerating partner integrations with inference platforms to provide a turnkey visibility layer (request-level traces, prompt provenance, and lightweight telemetry) without changing customer code.

We’d love to explore a formal integration with Redwood where LlamaWatch emits a small tracing payload that Redwood can surface in Console (per-route latency breakdown, token attribution, and prompt diffs). High-level asks:
- Quick technical sync to confirm headers/payload and sampling strategy
- Pilot with ~3 customers using LangChain and LlamaIndex adapters
- Optional co-marketing if pilot metrics look good

I attached a short telemetry spec and a sample SOW to this thread (see attachments). Are you available for a 30–45 min technical kickoff next week? We can also loop in Karthik from runtime/telemetry if that makes sense.

Thanks,
Olivia Harper
Head of Partnerships | LlamaWatch
[Attachment: LlamaWatch_TelemetrySpec_v1.csv (csv)]
[Attachment: LW_Redwood_SOW_draft.pdf (pdf)]

Subject: Re: Intro: LlamaWatch instrumentation - lightweight traces for LangChain/LlamaIndex

Hi Olivia — welcome and thanks for the note + attachments. Vanessa and I reviewed the spec quickly; I’ve looped Karthik (runtime/telemetry) for compatibility checks. A couple quick questions before the sync:

1) Sampling & payload size: what’s a realistic trace payload per request (KB)? We prefer < 2KB for sampled payloads to keep token overhead minimal.
2) Auth/ingestion: do you support a mutually authenticated endpoint (mTLS) or signed token-based ingestion? For Private customers we’ll need options that avoid public ingestion endpoints.
3) LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters: can your SDK be toggled at runtime (no rebuild) and disable KV capture for customers that need privacy?

We’re available for a 30-min technical sync Friday 2027-01-08 at 10:00 PT or Monday 2027-01-11 at 09:00 PT. Prefer to start with technical compatibility and then scope a pilot & SOW. Vanessa — can you take PS ownership if we move forward?

—Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Product Partnerships | Redwood Inference

From: Olivia Harper <olivia@llamawatch.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Riley <ben@llamawatch.ai>
Date: Wed, 6 Jan 2027 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro: LlamaWatch instrumentation - lightweight traces for LangChain/LlamaIndex

Thanks Stephanie — answers inline and attaching a compact payload example.

1) Sampling & payload size: typical sampled payload (pointer + minimal context) ~ 800–1200 bytes. Full verbose capture (including tokens and embeddings) is 6–12KB but we send that only when customers opt into deep debugging. Default pilot config keeps payloads sub-1.2KB.

2) Auth/ingestion: we support signed JWT ingestion (recommended) and mTLS for enterprise/private deployments. We’ll share TLS cert instructions in the onboarding doc.

3) Runtime toggle: yes — our adapters for LangChain and LlamaIndex expose a runtime flag and environment variable so customers can turn capture on/off without a rebuild. KV capture is an opt-in boolean; default is off.

Attached: compact_payload_example.json (small sample), LlamaWatch_TelemetrySpec_v1.csv (spec), LW_Redwood_SOW_draft.pdf (SOW).

If that looks good, Friday 01/08 10am PT works for us.

Olivia

[Attachment: compact_payload_example.json (json)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Olivia Harper <olivia@llamawatch.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 7 Jan 2027 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro: LlamaWatch instrumentation - lightweight traces for LangChain/LlamaIndex

Thanks Olivia — quick technical notes from the runtime side:

- Token attribution: we need an explicit mapping from your trace IDs to Redwood request IDs and token counts. We plan to surface per-route token delta in Console; please include token_count and token_attribution fields in the compact payload.
- KV cache/LLM state: we cannot accept raw KV contents for privacy. If customers opt-in to deep debugging, we’ll accept redacted KV diffs or hash-based fingerprints only. Add a header (X-LW-KV-Mode: none|hash|full) to indicate capture level.
- Quantized models: the runtime will sometimes serve int8 or 4-bit quantized variants; please confirm if payloads need model-arch metadata (e.g., model_variant: "gptj-quant-4bit") so we can correlate perf regressions.
- Sampling: recommend a sampling header (X-LW-Sample-Rate: 0.01) and a consistent sample_id to join traces with token-level logs.

If you can add those fields to the telemetry spec we’ll validate against our parser. Also propose a short acceptance test: 1) send 100 sampled requests through LangChain adapter; 2) verify tokens/timings in Redwood Console; 3) validate no PII in payloads.

Karthik
Principal Engineer, Runtime | Redwood Inference

- No raw KV content in payloads unless explicitly opted-in by the customer;
- Pilot customers report no noticeable latency increase (>20ms median).

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.
